g.text: UEFI Secure Boot & measured-boot auditor · read-only
DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK
Platform Key is an untrusted reference/test key (PKfail)
PK subject "CN=DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK". These AMI/IBV sample keys shipped across
many vendors and their private keys are public, so anyone can sign a KEK/db update or
a bootloader that this machine will trust (CVE-2024-8105).
Install the OEM firmware update that replaces the PK, or reset to setup mode and
enroll your own PK. Until then treat Secure Boot on this machine as bypassable.
Test / sample certificate trusted in KEK
"CN=Contoso Test Key - firmware lab" looks like a development key; images signed with
it will be allowed to boot.
Remove the certificate from KEK (firmware setup → Key Management) or apply the
`mokutil --disable-validation` was used: shim boots unsigned grub/kernels while
firmware still reports Secure Boot as enabled.
Run `mokutil --enable-validation` and confirm in MokManager on next boot.
Event log does not replay to the live PCR values
Replaying the firmware event log does not reproduce the TPM's PCRs 0-7. Either the log
is incomplete/tampered, or something extended firmware PCRs outside the log — both
break remote attestation and BitLocker/TPM-sealed secrets' assumptions.
Compare against a known-good boot of the same firmware version; update firmware;
investigate early-boot code if it persists.
Current UEFI revocation lists contain several hundred entries; fewer than 200
indicates published revocations have not been applied. Heuristic — confirm against
1 Machine Owner Key(s) enrolled in shim
